result:
Lint, format and mypy are clean and all 38 targeted tests pass. The full suite still has 37 failures and 15 errors, which I attribute to unrelated causes. That attribution rests on reading the failure reasons, because I couldn't run a baseline without `git stash`.

## Commands and summary lines

| # | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ruff check src tests` | `All checks passed!` |
| 2 | `ruff format --diff <5 files>` | First run showed 2 files to reformat (line-wrapping). I applied both by hand with Edit, and the rerun gave `5 files already formatted`. |
| 3 | `mypy` | `Success: no issues found in 274 source files` |
| 4 | targeted pytest set (repro, new tests, `test_references_helpers`, `test_references_integration`, `test_lint_tenant_scope`, `test_no_bare_tenant_guc_cast`) | `38 passed in 1.65s` |
| 5 | `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -rfE tests` | `37 failed, 1042 passed, 31 skipped, 52 warnings, 15 errors in 9.10s` |

- **Type-ignore comments:** mypy covers `src` only, and ruff has no unused-ignore rule, so nothing flagged the `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comments in the test file. I left them in place.
- **Run-to-run variation:** the earlier full run gave `34 failed … 16 errors`, so the failure total moves between runs (50 vs 52). The test database is shared and several existing tests use hard-coded emails, so this variation fits state leaking between tests.

## Failure attribution

I split the run by directory to get complete id lists:
- `tests/integration` + `tests/security`: `1 failed, 63 passed, 29 skipped`.
- `tests/unit`: `36 failed, 979 passed, 2 skipped, 15 errors`.

None of the failing files import or exercise `teams.references`, `refs_in`/`refs_out`, `memory_readable_by`, the write tool's references path, or alembic heads. Grep for those names finds only passing files, and a grep for revision-head assertions in `tests/` finds nothing.

| Failing ids | Reason | Class |
|---|---|---|
| `security/test_scope_enforcement.py::TestStatsToolScopes::test_stats_tool_requires_read_scope` | `assert -32601 == -32000` (tool method not found) | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_effective_access_recompute.py` (2) | `assert 2 == 1` on `path_count` / UEA rows (shared-DB leftovers) | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_refresh_team_access.py` (2) | `botocore NoCredentialsError` (needs AWS) | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_rbac_resolver.py::…inactive_member_denied` | `team_members_status_check` constraint violation | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_user_effective_team_access_schema.py::…cascade_delete_on_user` | `teams_created_by_tenant_id_fkey` FK violation on cleanup | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_slugs_schema.py::…pk_uniqueness_within_scope` | `InFailedSQLTransactionError` | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_team_role_assignments_schema.py::…role_key_mapped_to_role_id` | `'admin' == None` | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_roles_catalog.py` (3) | `12 == 7` and `13 == 12` (roles table has more rows than the test assumes), and `asyncpg.IntegrityError` doesn't exist | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_enterprise_schema.py` (5), `test_enterprise_teams_api.py` (15), `test_enterprise_mcp_tools.py` (4 + 1 teardown error) | team-creation fixtures, hard-coded emails, FK on tenant cleanup | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_team_api.py` (12 errors) | `tenants_email_key` duplicate on hard-coded `user1@example.com` | unrelated pre-existing |
| `test_spec2_slug_lookup.py` (1 error) | `fixture 'populate_user_effective_access' not found` | unrelated pre-existing |

I did not look at the individual tracebacks of every `test_enterprise_*` failure, so those rows are classified from the shared fixtures and the visible error messages.

Nothing is "caused by change", so no existing-code fixes were needed.

## Not done

- **Baseline comparison:** the work order said to attribute rather than stash, so I didn't produce a before/after failure diff. That means "no new failures" is argued from the failure reasons, not proven by a set difference.
- **Repro flip:** the repro test passed (it is in the 38).
